# dsh-plugin-session-token-stats
**English** | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web plugin that turns your real session logs into a token-usage dashboard:
total tokens, session count, a daily usage timeline, per-session breakdown with cache-hit rate, and
live CPU/memory monitoring.
It counts tokens only. There is no reliable billing API for these sessions, so the page deliberately
shows **no estimated cost and no budget** instead of presenting a guess as a fact.
## What it shows
- **Summary cards** — total tokens (uncached input / cache-hit input / output), sessions (turns plus

how many subagent sessions were merged), tokens used this month, and the overall cache-hit rate.
-
**Token timeline** — daily stacked bars for the last 7 / 30 / 90 days (uncached, cache hit, output).

Hover a bar for that day's exact counts; the range is a per-browser setting.
- **Per-session usage*
* — one row per **main conversation**, newest first. Subagent sessions are merged into the conversat
ion that spawned them (the whole `parentSession` chain is folded, including multi-level delegation)
and never listed separately. Select a row to expand the per-model breakdown, merged subagent count,

creation/last-activity timestamps, and session id.
- **CPU & memory** — system CPU usage with a 120-
second sparkline, 1/5/15-minute load average, DSH process CPU and RSS, system memory, core count, pr
ocess uptime, and host identity.
## Counting rules
The Host half reads durable session logs through `ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions()` / `readSession(id
)` and counts every `assistant/message` usage report:
| Field | Meaning |

| uncached input | `usage.inputTokens` (DeepSeek excludes cache hits from this field) |
| cache hit

| `usage.cacheReadTokens` |
| output | `usage.outputTokens` |
| total | uncached + cache hit + outpu

t (+ `cacheWriteTokens` where a provider reports it) |
| cache-hit rate | cache hit ÷ (uncached + ca

eWriteTokens` where a provider reports it) |
| cache-hit rate | cache hit ÷ (uncached + cache hit) |
Two deduplication rules keep the numbers honest:
1. **Fork / seeded sessions** — the log starts with a prefix copied from the parent session, whose u
sage was already billed there. Only events after `inheritedEventCount` are counted (the latest `sess

ion/title` is still read from the whole log).
2. **Subagent sessions** — `header.parentSession` iden
tifies the spawning conversation; sessions are grouped up that chain to the top-most main session an
d reported as one row.
Persisted sessions are immutable, so each log is read once and cached; live sessions are re-read on
every refresh. The first open decompresses and replay-validates every log (roughly 10–20 seconds for
500+ sessions) and reports `{ done, total }` progress while polling quickly; afterwards refreshes o
nly re-read running sessions.
## Requirements

- A DeepSeek Harness Web profile, `dsh >= 0.2.1-rc.2`.
- Host services `sessionQuery`, `webServer`,
and `connection` (all present in the shipped Web profile).
## Install

ide any shipped component.

After installation, reload the page; a bar-chart entry (**Token stats**) appears at the bottom of th

## Host routes
Both routes are same-origin and owner-authenticated through the Connection service (unauthenticated
→ `401`; missing Connection service → `403`, fail-closed):
- `GET /session-token-stats/data` — totals, daily buckets, grouped per-session aggregates, scan prog

ress.
- `GET /session-token-stats/live` — CPU / load / memory sample ring (1 Hz, last 120 samples).

## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Tests need no third-party dependencies. The Host suite drives `apply()` with a synthetic corpus thro
ugh a fake Cordis context (usage folding, peak/off-peak day buckets, inherited-prefix exclusion, sub
agent grouping, scan caching, route auth); the Client suite loads the browser bundle with a stub mod
ule loader and covers token formatting, cache-hit rate, timeline zero-fill, per-browser preferences,
and dictionary parity.
## Limitations
- The first scan of 500+ logs takes a few seconds (decompress + replay validation); later refreshes

only re-read running sessions.
- The timeline keeps 120 days; older usage still appears in session r

ows and totals but not in the daily chart.
- When a parent session is no longer in the local corpus

(archived or pruned), its subagent sessions become their own top-most row.
- Titles follow the lates

t `session/title` event, falling back to the first user message for older logs.
- No cost/budget is
shown by design; use the token breakdown if you want to price sessions yourself.
